title: The panel toggle sits in the window title bar, where a Mac keeps it
goal: The button that collapses the right hand panel sits inside the panel's own header, beside the word Layers. On a Mac that control belongs in the window's title bar at the top right, which is where Finder, Mail and Xcode all put it, and where a person's hand goes without thinking. Put it there. It also means the button does not disappear along with the thing it collapses.
notes: Asked by the user on 2026-09-06, and the honest answer to why not yet is that nothing has put anything in the title bar before. The editor window is declared hiddenTitleBar (Sources/Photonz/PhotonzApp.swift line 43), which hides the title and the bar but keeps the title bar AREA where the traffic lights live, so a toolbar item can still be placed there; this is the same arrangement Finder uses. Two routes: attach a SwiftUI toolbar with a trailing item to the editor scene, or add an NSToolbar to the window and place the control in it. Prefer whichever keeps the current look, which is no visible bar and no title text, since adding a toolbar can bring a background and a divider that would change the window. Check both what the traffic lights do at a narrow width and whether the item survives full screen. Supersedes the-panel-collapse-button-sits-in-the-panel-s-ow, which moved the button from the canvas into the panel header; that was the previous step and this replaces it, so fold in anything it left behind, in particular the corner rect other chrome avoids and the measure legend that used to park under the old position.
acceptance: The panel toggle sits at the trailing end of the window title bar, level with the traffic lights, and looks like a title bar control rather than a button placed on top of the canvas
It shows the panel's state and toggles it, keeps its tooltip and its keyboard shortcut, and still brings the panel back when it has closed itself on a narrow window
With the panel collapsed the button is still there in the same place, so the way back never moves
The title bar carries no other clutter, and the top of the canvas gains the room the old button occupied
The window keeps its current look: no visible title text and no bar drawn across the top, only the control
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the panel open and closed, at a wide and a narrow window, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Reviewed the idea before building. Walked it as a first-time user: the top right of a title bar is where Finder, Mail and Xcode keep this, so the hand goes there; nothing else in the window competes for that corner. Two routes weighed: a SwiftUI toolbar brings its own glass background and a separator on macOS 26, which is a bar drawn across the top of a window that deliberately has none, so it was rejected. A titlebar ACCESSORY drops one view into the title bar area with no toolbar and no chrome, which keeps the window exactly as it looks today. Shortest version that delivers the value: one button, one home, and BOTH old homes deleted (the panel header's and the canvas capsule's) rather than keeping a fallback, since two ways back is the thing being fixed.

Shipped. New Sources/Photonz/TitlebarPanelToggle.swift hangs an NSTitlebarAccessoryViewController (layoutAttribute .trailing) on the editor window carrying one SwiftUI button; installed from EditorView's background, only with a document open, so an empty window never shows a dead control. EditorState gained isInspectorAutoHidden and isInspectorShown: the flag used to be @State in EditorView and the title bar is outside that tree, so setInspectorVisible now clears it and one reading answers for everyone. Removed: the dock's collapseButton and its headerTrailingReserve/isDockScrolled machinery (LayersPanel), the canvas corner overlay and inspectorToggle (EditorView), EditorChromeLayout.inspectorToggleFrame/inspectorToggleSize, and the measure legend's corner-chrome clearing, which is now just the plain inset. 4267 tests green.

Two harness bugs found and fixed on the way, both blocking any title bar control from ever being tested. A walk only searched window.contentView, so a titlebar accessory was invisible to press and hover; and asking a BORDERLESS window for its titlebarAccessoryViewControllers raises, which the run loop swallows, stranding the walk with no error and no done.json (the tooltip a hover leaves up is such a window, so hover-then-press hung for 180s). One guarded helper, findAllInTitlebar, now serves all three searches. Added a toggleFullScreen action so full screen is checked rather than assumed; it also puts the window back to a regular app's collection behavior, because a walk's window is built while the probe is still a menu-bar accessory and AppKit stamps those fullScreenNone for life.

Verified on the probe with Screen Recording granted. panel-toggle-titlebar-walk (open, tooltip, close, reopen, shortcut both ways, measure key in the freed corner) and panel-toggle-narrow-walk (620pt window auto-collapses, real presses on the title bar button both ways) both pass; legend-corner-slots, layers-lazy-rows and dock-component-first still pass. Measured off the real capture: the traffic lights span y 18..45px and the glyph y 20..44px, so both centre on the same row; the lights' circle sits 9pt off the left edge and the button's 10pt off the right. Full screen: the title bar hides and the button with it, the shortcut still works, and coming back restores it. Contrast checked in both appearances; the canvas keeps a title bar safe area, so the button never sits over document pixels.

Shared code, not Next-only: the editor shell, the dock and the chrome layout are all shared files that Next has not forked, so Next gets this by construction and Current gets the same move. This is a relocation of existing chrome, not a new feature, so no flag.

The panel toggle now sits at the trailing end of the window's own title bar, level with the traffic lights, in the same place whether the panel is open or closed. Built as a titlebar accessory (Sources/Photonz/TitlebarPanelToggle.swift), not a toolbar, so the window keeps its look: no title text, no bar drawn across the top. Both old homes are gone: the dock's header button and the glass capsule that floated in the picture's corner, along with EditorChromeLayout.inspectorToggleFrame and the gap the measure key used to leave under it. Verified on the probe with Screen Recording: Scripts/playtest/panel-toggle-titlebar-walk.json and panel-toggle-narrow-walk.json, plus legend-corner-slots, layers-lazy-rows and dock-component-first as regressions; 4267 tests green. Measured off the capture, the traffic lights and the glyph centre on the same row. Full screen hides the title bar and the button with it, the way a Mac does for a window with no toolbar; the shortcut still works there, and that is filed in the audit. Two harness bugs fixed on the way that had made any title bar control untestable. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-panel-toggle-titlebar.json with five real captures.
